Q: Setting OrderNumber of rows in a table in SQL Server A:

Please try the following conceptual example.

SQL

-- DDL and sample data population, start
DECLARE @tbl TABLE  (country VARCHAR(100), country_code CHAR(2));
INSERT @tbl(country,country_code) VALUES 
('Afghanistan','AF'),
('Albania','AL'),
('Algeria','DZ'),
('United States of America ','US');
-- DDL and sample data population, end

SELECT * 
FROM @tbl
ORDER BY IIF(country_code = 'US', 'AA', country_code);

Output

country country_code
United States of America US
Afghanistan AF
Albania AL
Algeria DZ

Q: Preciseness of DRY Principle A:

The programmers who read your code after will thank you if you optimize for maintainability, not strict adherence to any particular dogma.

Please don't misunderstand. DRY is important, but you should temper it (or any other design pattern) with a variation on the simple check: "Does this make sense?". In the case of DRY, this would be something along the lines of "Are these actually related?".

If the answer is "yes", strongly implying that if one of the classes were to drop the text-transform:uppercase; the other would also, then by all mean extract it out.

If the answer is "no", then you'd actually be making it more difficult to maintain later because you'd need to undo the artificial coupling between the two classes.

In this case, simply having a laundry-list of the classes that use a particular attribute is fake DRY, because you are definitely repeating yourself. The repetition has simply moved from the attribute to the class.

Q: Add more spacing between different files in git diff A:

Super old post, but a simple solution is to alias a loop in your ~/.bashrc file

eg

alias gd='for f in $(git diff --name-only); do printf "\n\n\n ---------------------- %s ----------------------------------- \n" $f; git --no-pager diff "$f"; done'
